Let me think about this year the way I always do — start from what I did last year and adjust.

**My land breakdown (14 mu total):**
I keep stevia as my main cash crop because the contracting company pays decent money and my neighbors in Quzhou have been doing well with it. I put 6 mu in stevia. Then I have 4 mu for wheat-maize double crop (wheat in winter, maize in summer on the same land). Cotton takes my remaining 4 mu — I've grown it for 20+ years, the soil there is sandier and suits cotton better.

**Stevia (6 mu):** The buyer wants good dry leaf. Last year I used about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (25 kg bag, 15-15-15) per mu plus urea topdressing. That worked. I'll do the same — about 18 kg N, 8 kg P, 10 kg K. Stevia likes water, I irrigate 4-5 times from my well. Pests come on the young leaves — I spray 3 times. Expect 250 kg dry leaf per mu.

**Wheat (4 mu):** Standard practice here. Basal compound plus urea topdressing at returning-green stage. 15 kg N, 7 kg P, 5 kg K. Irrigate 3 times — winter, returning-green, grain-filling. One pesticide spray for aphids. Improved variety seed from the agri-station, Jimai type. 450 kg/mu is what I usually get.

**Maize (4 mu):** After wheat, rotary till and plant hybrid Zhengdan-style seed. 17 kg N, 5 kg P, 5 kg K. Two irrigations. Two sprays — for borer and armyworm. 550 kg/mu target.

**Cotton (4 mu):** Cotton eats fertilizer and needs potassium. 14 kg N, 7 kg P, 10 kg K. I irrigate 3 times. Cotton gets the most spraying — bollworm, aphids, mites — at least 5 times. Improved Bt variety. 260 kg seed cotton per mu.

I would rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than lose yield — that's always been my rule.
